newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks seen lower on lack of buying incentives.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen lower on lack of buying incentives.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are seen easing further on Thursday on a lack of buying incentives, and the sharply lower close on Wall Street overnight also dampened sentiment, brokers said.
"The Hang Seng Index is likely to test the support level of 14,500 today as sentiment is weak and there is no buyer around," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
The Hang Seng Index fell 88.44 points to close at 14,703.73 on Wednesday. Later the Hang Seng London Reference Index slipped 14.80 points to finish at 14,688.93.

Brokers believed profit-taking on red chips would continue in the face of weak Chinese stock markets and rumours that China's regulators are investigating irregularities among the managements of red chip companies.
"Selling pressure is expected on pricy red chips while individual low-priced China-affiliated stocks might find some support at these levels," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index plunged 226.04 points, or 6.86 percent, to 3,069.91 on Wednesday.
